category: Telegram mirror/leech bot: remote-URL fetcher with operator-side storage

free_tier.stated: Leech: upto 80 GB/link (4gb support); Yt-dlp: upto 80 GB/link; Mega.nz Link: upto 80 GB/link; Daily Limit: Unlimited".
free_tier.notes: Unlimited refers to the daily count of links, not to bytes in flight; each link is capped at 80 GB.

per_object_cap.stated: 80 GB per link on every mode: mirror, leech, yt-dlp and MEGA.

retention.stated: Not stated. A mirror lands in operator storage and a leech lands in the user's Telegram; no expiry is published for either.

egress.terms: The bot pulls from a remote URL and re-serves it: a mirror returns a link on the operator's host, a leech returns the file into the chat. No bandwidth figure or price is published.

interface_detail: A Telegram bot, not an HTTP service: the control channel is Telegram chat with @publicmirrorbot, and there is no documented REST endpoint. The bot's preview names a fallback bot and a support group rather than an API.
tooling: Telegram client only. Automating it means driving a Telegram user session, which is a real constraint for a client that wants a script rather than a chat window.
chaining: A resolver for links a normal client cannot fetch: a MEGA or yt-dlp URL goes in, a direct file comes out, and it bypasses the per-host limits a downloader would otherwise meet. It is the human-shaped version of what a debrid subscription does, with an 80 GB per-link ceiling instead of a monthly one.

limits.value: 80 GB per link (mirror, leech, yt-dlp, MEGA)
daily limit stated as unlimited; concurrent-task and queue limits are not published

limits_note: The 80 GB figure is generous for a free bot and is the only hard number the operator publishes. Nothing is said about how many tasks may run at once, which is where a shared public bot actually queues.
binding_note: At 1 TiB a month the link ceiling is what stops a single transfer: 80 GB is about 12 links to the monthly target, so a 1 TiB archive has to be split. The daily count is explicitly unlimited, so it cannot bind.

identity_cost.detail: A Telegram account is the only gate: any phone number that can receive the signup code. No email, payment or identity document is asked for by the bot.

reliability_note: A shared public bot with no SLA and an operator who publishes limits in a channel post rather than a page: the 80 GB figure can change in one message, and the bot's uptime depends on somebody else's server.
confidence_note: Moving to documented needs the numbers on a stable page; moving to measured needs one 80 GB job run and read.

evidence.proved: the limits post verbatim: 80 GB per link on mirror, leech, yt-dlp and MEGA, and 'Daily Limit: Unlimited'
the bot exists as 'Mirror Leech Bot 3' and links @PublicMirrorLeechGroup and @PublicMirrorLeechUpdates as its group and channel
3,088 members and 380 online, which is the scale signal for a public bot's queue

notes: Classified as a service because it resolves and fetches remote URLs rather than mirroring an account: a client hands it a URL and gets bytes back. The account-mirror bots in the same ledger were not recorded, because they only drive somebody's own cloud account.
